          Bayern Munich vs Borussia Dortmund Prediction: Bundesliga Der Klassiker Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 29, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
This season's first edition of Der Klassiker takes place at the Allianz Arena with the two teams sitting level on points. We look ahead to the game with our Bayern Munich vs Borussia Dortmund prediction and preview.
It has been a positive week for everyone connected to Bayern Munich.

Harry Kane‘s Ballon d'Or triumph made him the first Bayern player to win football's top individual prize since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981, and the first Bundesliga recipient overall since Borussia Dortmund icon Matthias Sammer in 1996.

And things could get better for Bayern on Saturday, as they host Borussia Dortmund in Der Klassiker, which will be Kane's first game back since Monday's award ceremony. He was an unused substitute for Wednesday's 6-1 DFB-Pokal rout of Magdeburg.
Both teams have 17 points on the board after seven matchdays (both W5 D2), making them the only remaining unbeaten teams in the 2026-27 Bundesliga.

In two of the last three Bundesliga seasons, Bayern have handed BVB their first defeat of the campaign – they beat their rivals 2-1 in Munich on Matchday 7 of 2025-26, having triumphed 4-0 in Dortmund on MD10 of 2023-24.

In addition, Bayern are unbeaten in their last 21 league matches when playing as leaders against the side in second place (W13 D8), the longest such run by any team in Bundesliga history. Their last defeat in such a fixture came in January 2015, 4-1 at Wolfsburg.

And when you have the best player in the world on your side, you will always feel you have a chance. Kane has scored six goals in his six previous Bundesliga matches against Dortmund, including a hat-trick in his first Klassiker (November 2023) and a brace in February.

But Kane, clearly, is not the only star attacker that Niko Kovac's visitors must keep a close eye on. His nine goal involvements (four goals, five assists) in the Bundesliga this season is only matched by teammate Michael Olise (six goals, three assists).
Olise has recorded at least one goal and one assist in three of his last four Bundesliga matches, as many games with one of each as he managed in his previous 23 outings.

The former Crystal Palace star scored the clinching goal as Bayern defeated Freiburg 3-1 last weekend, with assistant coach Aaron Danks overseeing that game in place of Vincent Kompany, who is still recovering after collapsing at the club's training ground last week.
Kompany was discharged from hospital on Wednesday and is “doing well” according to club director Max Eberl, but it will be a while longer before the Belgian is back in the dugout as he recovers.
Bayern's 25 goals this season is the most in the Bundesliga, while they also boast the second-best defensive record in the division with six goals conceded.

And a remarkable 18 of those 25 goals have been scored in their first three home matches of the season, a new record by any club at this stage of a campaign. Bayern have scored at least five goals in each of their last four Bundesliga home games dating back to last season, the first time they have done so in their history.

Dortmund, though, are the one Bundesliga side with a better defence than Bayern; in fact, their four goals conceded is the fewest by any team in Europe's top five leagues. BVB kept five clean sheets in their opening seven matches, equalling their club record set in 2017-18 and 2020-21.

Maximilian Beier could be their player to watch, having tallied 13 Bundesliga goal involvements in 2026 (seven goals, six assists). The only German player with more this year is Deniz Undav (17), and 11 of Dortmund's 12 Bundesliga goals this campaign have been scored while Beier has been on the pitch.
This will be the 141st competitive meeting between Bayern and Dortmund since the formation of the Bundesliga in 1963 – it is the most-played fixture in German professional football.
Bayern have suffered more defeats against Dortmund than they have versus any other opponent in all competitions (33).

However, they have lost only one of their last 17 meetings (W13 D3 L1), suffering a 2-0 home defeat under Thomas Tuchel in March 2024, which virtually ended their title hopes as Bayer Leverkusen went on to claim the trophy.

Bayern did the double over BVB last season, triumphing 2-1 at home last October and earning a thrilling 3-2 success on the road in February, with Joshua Kimmich scoring an 87th-minute winner in the latter game.
